title: Use of multiple indicators multiple causes (MIMIC) method to investigate quantitative inference in socioeconomic determinants on motorcyclist stress
author: Meilinda, Sugiarto, et al.

steps.title: Define routes and allocate participants
steps.instruction: Select two route categories: primary arterial road (Jalan T. Nyak Arief to Jalan T. Muhammad Daud Bereueh) and secondary arterial road (Jalan Syiah Kuala and Jalan T. Hasan Dek to Jalan Dr. Mr. Mohd Hasan). Recruit 50 participants, assign 25 to each route, and schedule data collection with three to four participants per day.

steps.title: Brief participants and verify safety
steps.instruction: Hold a briefing session informing participants of study objectives, procedures, and safety requirements, confirming they hold a valid SIM C driving license and wear protective helmets.

steps.title: Collect sociodemographic questionnaire
steps.instruction: Have participants complete a questionnaire capturing age, gender, education level, occupation, travel purpose, average daily trips, household income, driving experience, daily driving duration, number of motorcycles owned, and possession of a driving license.

steps.title: Record baseline heart rate
steps.instruction: Fit each participant with a Polar Vantage V2 smartwatch and record baseline heart rate for 10 min before driving.

steps.title: Conduct driving trial
steps.instruction: Instruct participants to drive their motorcycles along the assigned route at an average speed of 60 km/h.

steps.title: Extract heart rate data
steps.instruction: After the drive, export the recorded heart rate data from the Polar Vantage V2 using the Polar Flow application.

steps.title: Analyze data with MIMIC
steps.instruction: Organize the extracted heart rate data and perform quantitative inference using the Multiple Indicators Multiple Causes (MIMIC) method.
